evidence.excerpt: Static best-before labelling does not reflect the actual quality state of perishable foods subjected to variable cold-chain conditions. This paper reports a feasibility study for implementing sensor-based dynamic remaining shelf-life (RSL) labelling on raspberry and blueberry consignments exported from Serbia. Time-temperature indicator (TTI) labels from two commercial suppliers were benchmarked against data-logger-calibrated predictive model outputs for Botrytis growth and total aerobic count across 24 simulated and 16 real export consignments. TTI colour-response kinetics were characterised at 0, 4, 8, and 12 °C and integrated into an RSL calculation algorithm using an Arrhenius-based temperature dependence model. Agreement between TTI-derived RSL and model-derived RSL was within ±1.2 days for 79% of consignments, which was deemed commercially acceptable by participating exporters. A cost–benefit analysis estimated that TTI-based RSL labelling could reduce consignment rejection rates at destination by 18–24%, yielding a positive return on investment for exporters operating above 50 tonnes per season. Regulatory and labelling compliance considerations under EU food law are discussed, along with the data requirements for formal TTI validation. The study supports the case for piloting RSL labelling in the Serbian berry export sector as part of a broader cold-chain quality assurance programme.
